questions.q: According to Luke 1:30-33, which angel announced the birth of Jesus Christ to the Virgin Mary?
options: Angel Michael
Angel Gabriel
Angel Uriel
Angel Raphael
questions.explain: The Annunciation was carried out by the angel Gabriel. According to Luke 1:26-33, God sent the angel Gabriel to Nazareth to a virgin named Mary to announce that she would conceive and give birth to Jesus.

questions.q: In Matthew 1:22-23, the prophet Isaiah foretold that the child's name would be called *Emmanuel*, which translated means:
options: Savior of the world
The Prince of Peace
God with us
King of the Jews
questions.explain: Matthew 1:23 quotes Isaiah's prophecy: "Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name Immanuel" (which means, God with us).

questions.q: Based on the biblical account in Luke 2, why did Joseph and Mary travel from Nazareth to Judea before the birth of Jesus?
options: To attend the annual Passover feast in Jerusalem
To escape from King Herod's decree
To register for the census commanded by Caesar Augustus
To visit their relative Elizabeth in the hill country
questions.explain: Caesar Augustus issued a decree that a census should be taken of the entire Roman world. Joseph went to his ancestral town of Bethlehem in Judea to register with Mary (Luke 2:1-5).

questions.q: Who were the first group of people to receive the joyful news of Jesus' birth directly from the angels, according to Luke 2:8-20?
options: The Wise Men from the East
The Shepherds tending their flocks
The High Priests in the temple
The Roman Soldiers stationed in Judea
questions.explain: An angel of the Lord appeared to shepherds who were living out in the fields nearby, keeping watch over their flocks at night, to announce the birth of the Savior.

questions.q: In Isaiah 9:6-7, several titles are prophesied for the coming Messiah. Which of the following is **NOT** one of those titles?
options: Wonderful Counselor
Mighty God
Lily of the Valley
Everlasting Father
questions.explain: Isaiah 9:6 states: "...and his name shall be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace." 'Lily of the Valley' is found in Song of Solomon 2:1, but not in this specific prophecy.

questions.q: During the visit of the wise men from the East (Matthew 2:1-22), which king was ruling in Judea and felt threatened by the news of a new "king of the Jews"?
options: King Saul
King Agrippa
King Solomon
King Herod
questions.explain: King Herod (Herod the Great) was the ruler of Judea at the time. When the wise men asked about the newborn King of the Jews, Herod was deeply troubled and secretly plotted to kill the child.

options: Gold
Silver
Frankincense
Myrrh
questions.explain: According to Matthew 2:11, the wise men opened their treasures and presented him with gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh. Silver was not mentioned.

questions.q: In Matthew 1:21, the angel instructed Joseph to name the child Jesus. What was the specific reason given for this name?
options: Because he would overthrow the Roman Empire
Because it was the traditional name of his ancestors
Because he would save his people from their sins
Because he would rebuild the temple in Jerusalem
questions.explain: The angel said, "She will bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins." The name Jesus (Yeshua) means 'The Lord saves'.

questions.q: From a Christian moral perspective, what is a primary value of maintaining virginity before marriage?
options: It guarantees that a person will marry a very wealthy spouse.
It honors God, ensures moral purity, and prevents premarital consequences like STDs.
It ensures the individual will eventually become a community leader.
It guarantees that a person will never experience temptation.
questions.explain: Maintaining virginity before marriage aligns with biblical teachings on sexual purity and self-control. Practically, it honors the sanctity of marriage and prevents issues like unwanted pregnancies and sexually transmitted diseases.

questions.q: According to Jewish law (Luke 2:21-24), when was Jesus officially circumcised and given His name?
options: On the very day he was born
On the eighth day after his birth
On the twelfth day after his birth
After forty days of purification
questions.explain: Luke 2:21 records that at the end of eight days, when he was circumcised, he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

questions.q: When presenting Jesus in the temple for the purification rites, Joseph and Mary offered a sacrifice. What did they offer, indicating their humble economic status?
options: A male lamb without blemish
A measure of fine flour and oil
A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons
A young calf
questions.explain: According to Luke 2:24, they offered a sacrifice according to what is stated in the Law of the Lord: "a pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons." This was the provision in Leviticus 12:8 for those who could not afford a lamb.

questions.q: Who was the righteous and devout man in the temple who took the infant Jesus in his arms and praised God because the Holy Spirit had promised he would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ?
options: Zechariah
Joseph of Arimathea
Nicodemus
Simeon
questions.explain: Simeon was waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him. He took the child Jesus in his arms and praised God, declaring that his eyes had seen God's salvation (Luke 2:25-32).

questions.q: During the presentation of Jesus in the temple, Simeon gave a troubling prophecy directly to Mary. What did he say?
options: That she would be exiled in Egypt for many years
That a sword will pierce through her own soul also
That she would lose her son in the wilderness
That her family would face extreme poverty
questions.explain: In Luke 2:34-35, Simeon blessed them and told Mary, "Behold, this child is appointed for the fall and rising of many in Israel... and a sword will pierce through your own soul also," foreshadowing Mary's grief at the crucifixion.

The tribe of Asher
The tribe of Levi
The tribe of Benjamin

questions.q: How is the prophetess Anna described in Luke 2 regarding her lifestyle and devotion?
options: She traveled from city to city preaching the gospel.
She worked as a servant keeping the holy of holies clean.
She did not depart from the temple, worshiping with fasting and prayer night and day.
She collected alms for the poor at the temple gate.
questions.explain: Luke 2:37 states that Anna was a widow until she was eighty-four and that "She did not depart from the temple, worshiping with fasting and prayer night and day."

questions.q: In Matthew 12:46-50, Jesus was told that his mother and brothers were waiting outside to speak to him. What was Jesus' profound teaching about the true meaning of "family"?
options: That biological ties are the only important connections in life
That whoever does the will of his Father in heaven is his brother, sister, and mother
That his family exclusively consisted of the twelve apostles
That family matters should always be resolved in private
questions.explain: Jesus stretched out his hand toward his disciples and redefined spiritual kinship by saying, "For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother" (Matthew 12:50).

questions.q: After a three-day search, Mary and Joseph finally found the young Jesus in the temple. What was he doing?
options: He was weeping because he was lost and hungry.
He was working alongside a carpenter making benches.
He was sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
He was offering sacrifices at the bronze altar.
questions.explain: Luke 2:46 says, "After three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions." Everyone who heard him was amazed at his understanding.

questions.q: How does Luke 2:51 describe Jesus' attitude and behavior toward his parents after they found him in the temple and returned to Nazareth?
options: He refused to return and insisted on living in the temple.
He went down with them and was submissive to them.
He returned with them but complained about living in Nazareth.
He became an independent adult and left his family completely.
questions.explain: Luke 2:51 confirms his obedience: "And he went down with them and came to Nazareth and was submissive to them. And his mother treasured up all these things in her heart."

questions.q: Ephesians 6:1-3 instructs children to obey their parents. Which of the following is the specific biblical promise attached to this commandment?
options: That they will become successful business owners in their community
That it may go well with them and they may live long in the land
That they will never experience trials or temptations
That they will instantly gain wisdom and understanding
questions.explain: Paul quotes the fifth commandment in Ephesians 6:1-3, saying, "'Honor your father and mother' (this is the first commandment with a promise), 'that it may go well with you and that you may live long in the land.'"

questions.q: According to Matthew 1:18-25, what was Joseph's initial decision when he discovered that Mary was with child before they came together?
options: He decided to report her to the high priest.
He resolved to divorce her quietly to avoid public disgrace.
He decided to marry her immediately.
He planned to banish her from the city of Nazareth.
questions.explain: Because Joseph her husband was a righteous man and did not want to expose her to public disgrace, he had in mind to **divorce her quietly**. (Matthew 1:19)

questions.q: When King Herod asked the chief priests and scribes where the Christ was to be born, which city did they name based on prophetic scriptures?
options: Nazareth of Galilee
Jerusalem
Bethlehem of Judea
Capernaum
questions.explain: They replied, "In **Bethlehem in Judea**," quoting the prophet Micah (Micah 5:2) who stated that a ruler would come from Bethlehem. (Matthew 2:5-6)

questions.q: What does the presentation of Jesus in the temple (Luke 2:21-24) reveal about his earthly parents, Joseph and Mary?
options: They were priests who served in the temple.
They were obedient observers of the Jewish Law.
They were extremely wealthy and influential.
They did not believe in the customs of Israel.
questions.explain: Joseph and Mary presented Jesus to the Lord and offered a sacrifice *"according to what is stated in the Law of the Lord."* This demonstrates their devotion and strict adherence to the religious laws of Moses.

questions.q: What action did the prophetess Anna take immediately after she saw the baby Jesus during his presentation in the temple?
options: She wept bitterly because of the prophecy of Simeon.
She anointed the baby with holy oil and left the temple.
She gave thanks to God and spoke about the child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.
She adopted the child so he could be raised as a priest.
questions.explain: Luke 2:38 records: "Coming up to them at that very moment, she gave thanks to God and spoke about the child to all who were looking forward to the redemption of Jerusalem."

questions.q: In Matthew 12:46-50, Jesus was teaching a crowd when he was informed that his mother and brothers were waiting for him outside. What was the context of this event?
options: They were bringing him his carpentry tools.
Jesus used the moment to explain that spiritual obedience is the basis of true kinship in God's kingdom.
Jesus rebuked the crowd and went home immediately.
They wanted him to pay the temple tax.
questions.explain: Jesus used this interruption as a teaching moment to redefine family. He pointed to his disciples and said, > "For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother."

questions.q: According to Luke 2:52, how did Jesus develop during his youth after returning to Nazareth?
options: He increased in wisdom and in stature, and in favor with God and man.
He became famous for leading rebellions against Rome.
He lived in the wilderness and only ate locusts and wild honey.
He refused to learn the carpentry trade and traveled constantly.
questions.explain: The biblical summary of Jesus' youth states exactly this: *"And Jesus increased in wisdom and in stature and in favor with God and man."* (Luke 2:52)
